correctness.rationale: The determinant-one companion update is a permutation. Its irreducible mod-two polynomial gives multiplication by a nonidentity element of F8, so primitive states reduce to a seven-cycle. Independently recomputed the two integer lifting certificates by iterating the update on basis states: det((M^7−I)/2)=87 and det((M^14−I)/4)=7569. The first square needs the separate second certificate; beyond it, normalized repeated squaring preserves the leading matrix modulo two. An invertible leading matrix cannot increase the valuation of a primitive vector, hence (M^(7·2^j)−I)v has coordinate valuation t+j+1 exactly. Cancelling 2^t reduces period to that of a primitive state at depth k−t. Since the period divides the first fixing iterate in this dyadic chain and is divisible by seven, it is exactly the claimed period. The shell contains 7·8^j states, giving 4^j cycles; the zero state is separately fixed, including at k=1. An independent exact fixed-point census through k=5 matched all cumulative counts and their differences.
residual_risks: The bounded fixed-point check corroborates the exact induction but is not the proof for general k.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A state of valuation t is the injective scalar image of a primitive state modulo 2^(k−t), and that identification commutes with M. Hence Brent implies period 7·2^(k−t−1). The shell cardinality divided by this period gives 4^j and summation gives the total; no new unlimited-depth recurrence theorem or substantial census remains.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A period of the scalar sequence for every n is exactly the period of its full consecutive state because it is generated by that state and exposes its three coordinates. Brent uses the reverse polynomial Q=1−2x−x²−x³; it is irreducible mod two and has principal period seven there. Reversing between Q and the companion polynomial replaces multiplication by an inverse and leaves order unchanged.

originality.rationale: Brent's published general maximal-period criterion and equality of principal and primitive-seed periods cover this claim by a direct corollary. The only evaluation required is at modulus eight, followed by cancelling scalar powers of two and dividing a shell cardinality by the common period. This is verified prior implication, not a claim that the Pell table already appeared verbatim or that an unavailable paper covers it.
residual_risks: The cited 2018 Pell-period text and Ward's earlier discussion were not independently inspected. Neither access limitation is needed for the finding of prior coverage by Brent.

value.rationale: The all-seed cycle spectrum is a natural invariant, but here the finished claim is the routine small-modulus specialization of an existing theorem about all primitive seeds. The extension to every seed is exactly scalar cancellation and shell division, and the integer certificates are elementary evaluations for this fixed companion. The self-contained argument may be useful exposition; it does not establish a distinct scientific finding warranting acceptance under the exact-invariant standard.
residual_risks: No broader recurrence theorem or non-routine new invariant is part of this frozen claim; no repair was supplied.
